acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The petitioner, Smt.Sohani, has preferred a revision petition for the relief of setting aside an order dismissing her application under Section 125 Cr. P.C. and awarding maintenance to her.

legal_principles.principle: The Magistrate is prima facie satisfied with regard to the performance of marriage in proceedings under S.125, Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: From the evidence which is led if the Magistrate is prima facie satisfied with regard to the performance of marriage in proceedings under S.125, Cr.P.C. which are of summary nature strict proof of performance of essential rites is not required.
cited_cases: S.Sethurathinam Pillai vs. Barbara alias Dolly Sethurathinam, (1971) 3 SCC 923

legal_principles.principle: Maintenance under section 488 (similar to Section 125, Cr.P.C.) cannot be denied where there was some evidence on which conclusion for grant of maintenance could be reached.
legal_principles.held: It was held that order passed under Section 488 is a summary order which does not finally determine the rights and obligations of the parties;
cited_cases: S.Sethurathinam Pillai vs. Barbara alias Dolly Sethurathinam, (1971) 3 SCC 923

legal_principles.principle: The term 'wife' occurring in Section 125, Cr.P.C. is to be given a very wide interpretation.
legal_principles.held: This is so stated in the following manner: A broad and expansive interpretation should be given to the term 'wife' to include even those cases where a man and woman have been living together as husband and wife for reasonably long period of time,
cited_cases: Chanmuniya vs. Virendra Kumar Singh Kushwaha & Anr.
